quizzes.title: Pygame Fundamentals
quizzes.description: Test your knowledge of Pygame core concepts and this project's simulation

questions.question: What is the target frame rate (FPS) for the Lab 8 Pygame simulation?
questions.explanation: The simulation runs at 60 FPS as specified in the WINDOW_WIDTH and FPS constants.

questions.question: Which class represents a square entity in the simulation?
questions.explanation: MovingSquare is a dataclass that stores position, velocity, size, color, and lifecycle data.

questions.question: What function is responsible for rendering one frame in the Pygame simulation?
questions.explanation: The draw_scene() function clears the background, draws squares, and flips the display buffer.

questions.question: What is the main entry point for running the Pygame simulation?
questions.explanation: The run() function orchestrates the main game loop and is called from __main__.

questions.question: Which parameter controls the blend between random jitter and directed chase behavior?
questions.explanation: CHASE_WEIGHT (default 0.55) controls how much the movement blends jitter vs. chase toward larger squares.

quizzes.title: Physics & Movement
quizzes.description: Questions about physics simulation, collision detection, and movement mechanics

questions.question: What does the BOUNCE_DAMPING coefficient (0.82) represent?
questions.explanation: BOUNCE_DAMPING (0.82) means squares retain 82% of velocity after wall collision, losing 18% as energy dissipation.

questions.question: What is the detection radius for finding chase targets?
questions.explanation: DETECTION_RADIUS is set to 220.0 pixels, limiting target acquisition range.

questions.question: How does square size affect maximum velocity in the simulation?
questions.explanation: Smaller squares move faster due to speed_scale = BASE_SQUARE_SIZE / size, creating size-based speed scaling.

questions.question: What happens when a square reaches the end of its lifespan?
questions.explanation: The rebirth_square() function resets a square to a new random state when age >= lifespan.

questions.question: What is the minimum size difference (MIN_SIZE_DELTA) required to chase a target?
questions.explanation: MIN_SIZE_DELTA is set to 6, preventing squares from chasing targets unless they're at least 6 pixels larger.

quizzes.title: Architecture & Design
quizzes.description: Test your understanding of the project architecture and system design patterns

questions.question: How many independent runtimes does the Lab 8 project have?
questions.explanation: The project has 2 independent runtimes: the Pygame simulation and the Code Explorer web utility.

questions.question: Which port does the Code Explorer server run on?
questions.explanation: The Code Explorer runs on localhost:8000 using ThreadingHTTPServer.

questions.question: What is the algorithmic complexity of the nearest-target search?
questions.explanation: The _find_nearest_larger_target() function iterates through all squares, making it O(n²) per frame (n for each square).

questions.question: Which data structure stores the main simulation state?
questions.explanation: Simulation state is stored as a List[MovingSquare], which is updated in-place each frame.

questions.question: What is the resolution of the Pygame window?
questions.explanation: WINDOW_WIDTH and WINDOW_HEIGHT are set to 800 and 600 respectively.

quizzes.title: Code Organization
quizzes.description: Questions about the codebase structure, functions, and best practices

questions.question: What does the _make_square() function do?
options: Deletes a square from the list
Creates one square with random attributes
questions.explanation: _make_square() creates a single MovingSquare with randomized position, velocity, size, color, and lifespan.

questions.question: Which function computes the center point of a square?
questions.explanation: The _center() function returns (x + size/2, y + size/2), computing the square's center coordinates.

questions.question: What does handle_events() return?
options: The quit status (True = keep running, False = quit)
questions.explanation: handle_events() returns False when pygame.QUIT is triggered, signaling the game loop to exit.

questions.question: Type annotations in the project use which feature?
questions.explanation: The project uses 'from __future__ import annotations' for forward-compatible type hints.

questions.question: What method scales velocity based on square size?
questions.explanation: Speed scaling uses speed_scale = BASE_SQUARE_SIZE / size, making smaller squares faster.

quizzes.title: Code Explorer Utility
quizzes.description: Questions about the web-based Code Explorer tool

questions.question: What port does the Code Explorer server listen on?
questions.explanation: The Code Explorer runs on 127.0.0.1:8000 and can be accessed at http://127.0.0.1:8000

questions.question: Which API endpoint returns the repository file tree?
questions.explanation: GET /api/tree returns all files, metadata, and repository summary.

questions.question: How do you retrieve the content of a specific file?
questions.explanation: GET /api/file?path=<relative_path> returns the file content with language detection.

questions.question: Which directories are excluded from the Code Explorer file listings?
questions.explanation: ignored_names = {'.git', '.venv', '__pycache__', '.DS_Store'} are filtered out for a cleaner view.

questions.question: What type of files does Code Explorer refuse to serve?
questions.explanation: Binary files are rejected; only text files matching TEXT_EXTENSIONS or named README/LICENSE are served.

quizzes.title: Advanced Pygame Concepts
quizzes.description: Deep dive into Pygame mechanics and the simulation system

questions.question: How is square opacity calculated in the rendering function?
questions.explanation: alpha = int(255 - ratio * 175) where ratio = age/lifespan, creating a visual fade effect as squares age.

questions.question: What is dt_seconds in the update loop?
options: Delta time: milliseconds since last frame / 1000
questions.explanation: dt_seconds = clock.tick(FPS) / 1000.0 converts milliseconds to seconds for frame-rate-independent physics.

questions.question: What is the purpose of IDLE_WAIT_MS in the main loop?
options: Limit CPU usage when no events pending
questions.explanation: IDLE_WAIT_MS (1 ms) pauses when no events are pending, reducing CPU usage during idle periods.

questions.question: How does the chase logic calculate direction to target?
options: dx, dy = tx - sx, ty - sy; normalized
questions.explanation: Direction is computed as (dx, dy) = (target_x - chaser_x, target_y - chaser_y), then normalized for unit direction.

questions.question: What does the velocity clamping do in update_squares()?
options: Caps velocity magnitude based on square size
Resets velocity to zero each frame
questions.explanation: Velocity is clamped to [-max_speed, max_speed] where max_speed = BASE_MAX_JITTER_SPEED * speed_scale.
